key_insight: This paper introduces MUSE, a benchmark designed to test how well large vision-language models understand educational, artistic, and culturally rich visual content in situated learning settings. It highlights that current models are not yet sufficiently evaluated for the kind of multi-modal reasoning needed in AI-assisted language learning.
problem_solved: Existing vision-language benchmarks mostly focus on real-world photos or narrow educational tasks, leaving a gap in evaluating how models interpret art-like imagery, emotional tone, cultural meaning, and context in classroom-style learning scenarios.
method: Build a benchmark tailored to situated education and AI-assisted language learning.
Assess models on multi-modal understanding of artistic imagery, including semantic, affective, and cultural interpretation.
Evaluate visual-context reasoning to measure whether models can support meaningful educational interaction.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, MUSE provides a more realistic testbed for assessing whether vision-language models are truly ready for educational use. It can guide model improvement, benchmark selection, and safer deployment in language-learning and tutoring applications.

paper_title: MUSE: Benchmarking Large Vision-Language Models on Multi-Modal Understanding in Situated Education
paper_authors: Luyao Zhu, Xun Wei Yee, Wei Li, Mun Thye Mak, Wee Siong Ng
